assumptions: The phi tag is the classification for PHI tables; the customer must create and apply it
users.org_id is the tenant field for $auth.org_id
patients is the only table where org_id-based tenant filtering applies; appointments and clinical_notes have no org_id
Field names ssn, dob, insurance_member_id and diagnosis are unique enough that table.field_attribute_required and table.tag_required match only the intended tables
record_audit_event is the only approved writer of audit_log, per the table and function comments
confusions: CONF-012 template fixes tag confidential, but CONF-010 template takes its tag from the customer; I changed CONF-012 to phi for consistency, and the skill does not say whether a template's preset tag is a fill or a fixed value
The parse output omits severity medium from the printed policy (default value), which looked like a dropped line on first read
The skill says a dotted field name selects nested fields but the template examples use table-qualified names; unclear when table.field is needed in db.output_fields_forbidden
Scope tables param on object.auth_required is in the scope list, but the template for AUTH-010 has no scoping example, so I had to infer how it combines with the check
table_selector shape for db.where_constraint_required is documented only as object{names, tag, has_field, has_fk_to}; no example value given
wished_for: A guide to using scope params (tables, tags, api_groups) on templates such as AUTH-010, with a PHI example
A HIPAA framework mapping listing which checks cover which safeguard, and which safeguards have no check
An example of db.where_constraint_required with table_selector
A read-only way to see which objects a rule would match before a push, or a dry-run that does not require evaluate
A note that a tag not on any table produces a warning at parse time, to be called out in the template
parse_errors_seen: CONF-010.R1: table_tags phi is on no table in this workspace (warning, expected until tagging)
why_confidence: The eight policies cover the checkable parts of the ask: login and tenant access for PHI endpoints, sensitive marking, field minimisation, log hygiene and audit writes. Two are inert until the customer tags tables phi (CONF-010, CONF-012 findings only). Most HIPAA requirements (BAAs, risk analysis, training, encryption, retention, breach notice) have no check. Nothing has been evaluated, so all matches are predictions from reading the code, and the policies cannot make the workspace HIPAA-safe.
